lessons.title: Writing : essay, letter, report, summary
lessons.programRef: Tle — Anglais : expression écrite (à vérifier sur le texte officiel)
lessons.author: CastBridge (brouillon IA)
lessons.source: Rédaction originale ; textes d'exemple écrits pour CastBridge ; à relire par un enseignant
objectives: Rédiger une lettre formelle ou un report.
Résumer un texte en respectant la limite de mots.
Utiliser des connecteurs variés et un registre soutenu.
reviewNotes: Types d'écrits demandés au Bac d'anglais (essay, lettre, report, summary) : à vérifier sur le texte officiel pour les séries A, C, D.
Formules de lettre britanniques (faithfully / sincerely) ; l'usage américain diffère : à signaler par l'enseignant.
Longueurs de production (mots) : repères indicatifs, à adapter au barème officiel.

blocks.title: Trois productions écrites
blocks.md:
Au Bac d'anglais, on peut vous demander : un **essay** (texte argumentatif), une **lettre formelle** ou un **report**, ou un **summary** (résumé). Chaque forme a ses codes : structure, registre, connecteurs.

Règle commune : un plan clair, des phrases complètes, un anglais **correct et soutenu** (pas de contractions ni d'argot dans les écrits formels).

blocks.title: L'argumentative essay
blocks.md:
**Introduction** : accroche (hook), contexte, **thesis statement** (votre position).
**Corps** : 2 ou 3 paragraphes, chacun avec *topic sentence* (idée), explication, **exemple**, lien avec la thèse.
**Counter-argument** : une objection puis sa réfutation (*Some people argue that… However…*).
**Conclusion** : reformuler la thèse, résumer, ouvrir (*In conclusion…*). Pas d'idée nouvelle.

blocks.title: Connecteurs (linkers)
blocks.md:
- **Ajout** : firstly, moreover, in addition, what is more.
- **Opposition** : however, but, on the other hand, whereas, although.
- **Cause / conséquence** : because, since, as a result, therefore.
- **Exemple** : for instance, for example, such as.
- **Conclusion** : in conclusion, to sum up, all in all.
Varier les connecteurs, mais toujours avec **sens**.

blocks.caption: Disposition d'une lettre formelle britannique.
blocks.alt: Un cadre figurant une lettre : adresse de l'expéditeur et date à droite, destinataire à gauche, Dear Sir or Madam, objet, bloc de texte « Purpose, details, request », puis Yours faithfully et la signature.

blocks.title: La lettre formelle
blocks.md:
**Disposition** : adresse de l'expéditeur, date, destinataire, formule d'appel, objet (*Re:* ou *Subject:*), corps, formule de politesse, signature.
**Formules** : *Dear Sir or Madam* → *Yours faithfully* ; *Dear Mr Tabi* → *Yours sincerely*.
**Expressions** : *I am writing to apply for / to complain about / to enquire about…* ; *I would be grateful if you could…* ; *I look forward to hearing from you.*
Pas de contractions.

blocks.title: Le report
blocks.md:
Un **report** informe et recommande, avec des **intertitres**.
- En-tête : *To / From / Date / Subject*.
- **Introduction** : but du rapport.
- **Findings** (constats), en paragraphes ou puces.
- **Conclusion** puis **Recommendations** (*I recommend that… / It would be advisable to…*).
Style : neutre, impersonnel, phrases courtes, temps du présent ou du passé selon l'enquête.

blocks.title: Le summary
blocks.md:
1. Lire deux fois ; souligner les **idées principales**.
2. Écarter exemples, citations, répétitions, détails.
3. **Reformuler** avec ses propres mots (synonymes, autres constructions).
4. Relier les idées par des **connecteurs**.
5. Respecter la **limite de mots** (compter) ; garder le même temps et la 3e personne ; aucune opinion personnelle.

blocks.title: Exemple 1 : un summary
blocks.statement: Text (fictional): « Every September, young people crowd the bus station in Bafoussam. Many hope to find work in Douala or Yaoundé. Clarisse, 18, is one of them. « In the village I helped my aunt in the fields, but I want to learn a trade, » she says. Her cousin has promised her a bed, not a job. She knows that city life is expensive and that nothing is guaranteed. Still, she is determined. » Summarise in about 25 words.

steps.md: **Idées principales** : (1) des jeunes migrent vers les villes pour travailler ; (2) Clarisse veut apprendre un métier ; (3) elle connaît les risques mais reste décidée.
**Détails écartés** : la gare de Bafoussam, la tante, le cousin, le lit.
**Rédaction** : on reformule et on relie les idées. Puis on compte les mots : cible 22 à 28.

blocks.answer: « Young people go to cities hoping for work. Clarisse wants to learn a trade; she knows city life is costly and uncertain, yet she is determined. » (26 words)

blocks.title: Exemple 2 : une lettre formelle (corps)
blocks.statement: Write the opening and the closing of a letter to the Mayor about uncollected rubbish in your neighbourhood.

steps.md: **Ouverture** : *Dear Sir or Madam, Re: Uncollected rubbish in Bastos* (objet). Puis : *I am writing to complain about the rubbish that has not been collected in our street for two weeks.*
**Demande** : *I would be grateful if you could send a collection team as soon as possible.*
**Clôture** : *I look forward to hearing from you. Yours faithfully, A. Mbarga.* (Dear Sir or Madam → faithfully)

blocks.answer: Une lettre formelle : objet, intention claire, demande polie, formule finale correspondant à l'appel.

blocks.title: Les pièges de l'expression écrite
blocks.md:
- **Contractions** (don't, I'm) et familiarités dans une lettre formelle.
- **Yours sincerely** après *Dear Sir/Madam* (c'est *faithfully*).
- Un essay **sans thèse** ou sans exemples.
- Résumé **trop long** ou avec des opinions.
- **Traduire du français** mot à mot (faux amis : *actually* ≠ actuellement, *to assist* ≠ assister à).
- Oublier de **relire** : accords, temps, orthographe.

items: Écrire chaque semaine un paragraphe argumentatif de 80 mots sur un sujet d'actualité locale.
Se constituer un tableau des formules d'ouverture et de clôture de lettres.

exercises.prompt: Associez chaque expression à sa fonction.
pairs: I am writing to complain about…
Clôture après « Dear Sir or Madam »
exercises.explanation: Chaque expression structure le texte : ouvrir, ajouter, opposer, illustrer, conclure.

exercises.prompt: A letter begins « Dear Mr Tabi, ». Which closing is correct?
exercises.explanation: Avec un nom propre (Dear Mr Tabi) : Yours sincerely. Yours faithfully va avec Dear Sir or Madam.

exercises.prompt: True or false: contractions like « don't » are appropriate in a formal letter.
exercises.explanation: Faux. Dans un écrit formel, on écrit les formes pleines : *do not*, *I am*.

exercises.prompt: Write the introduction (about 50 words) of an essay on: « Social media do more harm than good to teenagers. » Include a hook, some context and a thesis statement.
exercises.model: Nowadays, it is hard to imagine a teenager without a phone in hand. Social media connect friends, but they also take up time and expose young people to bad influences. In my opinion, although they offer some benefits, social media do more harm than good to teenagers because they weaken concentration and expose them to false information.
exercises.explanation: L'introduction doit se terminer par la thèse : elle annonce la position défendue.

exercises.prompt: Text (fictional): « Every September, young people crowd the bus station in Bafoussam. Many hope to find work in Douala or Yaoundé. Clarisse, 18, is one of them. « In the village I helped my aunt in the fields, but I want to learn a trade, » she says. Her cousin has promised her a bed, not a job. She knows that city life is expensive and that nothing is guaranteed. Still, she is determined. » Summarise the text in about 25 words (22 to 28), in your own words. Write the number of words.
exercises.model: Young people go to cities hoping for work. Clarisse wants to learn a trade; she knows city life is costly and uncertain, yet she is determined. (26 words)
exercises.explanation: Un résumé garde les idées, supprime les détails et reste dans la limite de mots.

exercises.prompt: Situation: you are a student of Terminale. Your school library closes at 3 p.m. You want it to stay open until 5 p.m. You are going to write a formal letter to the Headteacher. Name: Alain Mbarga.

parts.explanation: Pour un destinataire non nommé ou une autorité : Dear Sir or Madam (ou Dear Headteacher). Le registre doit être formel.

parts.prompt: Write the first paragraph (purpose of the letter), 30 to 40 words.
parts.model: I am writing to request that the school library remain open until 5 p.m. on weekdays. At present, it closes at 3 p.m., which prevents many students from using its books and quiet space after lessons end.
parts.explanation: Un paragraphe d'ouverture dit tout de suite pourquoi on écrit.

parts.prompt: Write a second paragraph giving two reasons, a polite request, and the closing.
parts.model:
Firstly, many Terminale students need extra time to revise for the Baccalaureate. Secondly, those who live far away cannot study at home because of power cuts. I would therefore be grateful if you could consider extending the library's opening hours. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Alain Mbarga
rubric: Demande polie et formule de clôture correcte (1 point).
parts.explanation: Les deux raisons soutiennent la demande ; la formule finale correspond à l'appel.

mistakes: Yours sincerely après Dear Sir or Madam.

exercises.prompt: What goes with « Dear Sir or Madam » ?

choices: The position defended in the essay
exercises.explanation: La thèse est la position défendue, à la fin de l'introduction.

exercises.prompt: In a summary you should NOT include:
exercises.explanation: Un résumé reste fidèle au texte : aucune opinion.

exercises.prompt: READING COMPREHENSION. Text (fictional, written for this exercise): « In the small town where Esther grew up, the river was once the heart of the community. Women washed clothes there and children swam on Sundays. Over the years, waste from small factories made the water grey and unsafe. Last year Esther, now a nurse, began a campaign. She asked each family to stop throwing rubbish near the banks and she wrote to the council. Progress is slow, but fish have started to return. « Nature forgives, » she says, « if we stop hurting it. » »

parts.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
choices: A factory wins a prize for its waste.
A nurse campaigns to restore a polluted river.
parts.explanation: Le texte raconte la campagne d'Esther pour nettoyer le cours d'eau pollué.

parts.prompt: In « began a campaign », the word « campaign » means:
choices: an organised effort to achieve something
parts.explanation: Dans le contexte, une campagne est une action organisée pour atteindre un but (ici nettoyer la rivière).

parts.prompt: Why did the water become unsafe? Answer in your own words.
parts.model: The water became unsafe because small factories released waste into the river for years.
parts.explanation: La cause est donnée par la phrase « waste from small factories made the water grey and unsafe ».

parts.prompt: Quote one sentence showing that Esther's efforts are having some effect.
parts.model: « Progress is slow, but fish have started to return. »
parts.explanation: La citation doit prouver l'effet des efforts : le retour des poissons.

parts.prompt: What does Esther mean by « Nature forgives, if we stop hurting it » ? (about 30 words)
parts.model: Esther means that nature can recover from the damage we have done, provided that we stop polluting it. Her confidence comes from the fact that fish are already returning to the river.
rubric: Sens correct : la nature peut se rétablir (1 point).
Condition « if we stop » comprise (1 point).
parts.explanation: La phrase exprime une espérance conditionnelle : il faut cesser de polluer.

exercises.source: Exercice original, épreuve blanche style Bac
exercises.method: Idée générale, vocabulaire, reformulation, citation, interprétation.

exercises.prompt: LANGUAGE. Complete the sentences and rewrite as asked.

parts.explanation: Since + point de départ : present perfect.

parts.prompt: If she ____ harder last year, she would have passed.
parts.explanation: Condition irréelle du passé : if + past perfect.

parts.prompt: Rewrite: 1) I regret not studying more. (I wish…) 2) He had hardly left when it rained. (Hardly…) 3) People say he is rich. (He is said…)
parts.model: 1) I wish I had studied more. 2) Hardly had he left when it rained. 3) He is said to be rich.
parts.explanation: Trois transformations, trois structures étudiées dans les fiches du pack.

exercises.source: Exercice original, épreuve blanche style Bac
exercises.method: Choisir la structure selon le contexte.

exercises.prompt: WRITING. Choose the topic « Young people should stay in villages instead of moving to cities. Do you agree? » and write the beginning of an argumentative essay.

parts.prompt: Write the introduction (hook, context, thesis), 40 to 60 words.
parts.model: Every year, thousands of young people leave their villages for the city. Some find work; many do not. In my opinion, young people should not all move to cities, because villages also offer opportunities, especially in farming and in new technologies.
parts.explanation: Une introduction annonce la position défendue en 40 à 60 mots.

parts.prompt: Write one body paragraph with an argument, an example and a linker.
parts.model: Firstly, villages can provide work in agriculture. For example, a young farmer who uses a phone to check market prices can earn a better income. Moreover, this work helps feed the whole country. Therefore, staying in the village can be a wise choice.
parts.explanation: Un paragraphe suit le schéma : idée, exemple, lien.
